what_its_for: Phenazopyridine helps relieve the pain, burning, urgency, and frequent need to urinate that come with urinary tract infections (UTIs) or bladder irritation. It works like a local painkiller for your bladder and urinary tract. Important: this medicine does NOT treat the infection itself — you will still need an antibiotic if you have a UTI.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with a full glass of water. Always take it with food or after a meal to help avoid an upset stomach. Swallow the tablet whole. Do not crush or chew it. This medicine will turn your urine a bright orange or red color — this is completely normal and expected. It can also stain your underwear and contact lenses, so be careful.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 95 mg to 200 mg taken 3 times a day, after meals. Only take it for as long as your doctor tells you — usually no more than 2 days. Do not take it longer than directed without talking to your doctor. Always follow the exact dose on your prescription or product label.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist about a medication take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid wearing contact lenses while taking this medicine, as it can permanently stain them orange or yellow. Be aware that it will stain fabric, so consider wearing darker underwear or using panty liners. Avoid taking this medicine for longer than 2 days unless your doctor specifically tells you to. Do not use it as a substitute for an antibiotic — it only relieves symptoms and does not cure an infection.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you develop yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes (jaundice), your skin looks blue or pale, you have unusual tiredness or weakness, your urine turns a brownish color (different from the normal bright orange), you develop a skin rash or itching, you have stomach pain, or your symptoms do not improve or get worse. Also call if you notice swelling or you feel short of breath.
when_it_works: This medicine starts relieving pain, burning, and discomfort usually within 20 to 30 minutes of taking the first dose. Most people feel significant relief within the first day. Remember, it only treats the symptoms — if you have an infection, you must also take your full course of antibiotics as prescribed, even if you start feeling better.
special_populations: Older adults: Use with caution, as the kidneys may not work as well with age, which can increase the risk of side effects. Kidney or liver problems: Do not use this medicine if you have significant kidney or liver disease — talk to your doctor before taking it. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as safety has not been fully established. Children: Dosing in children is based on weight — always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions carefully for children.
